s00.note: t=0 locate fit the lying rod at ctr [0.577,0.004,0.013] (49.2 mm, rms 0.17 mm); this matches the t=0 frame and the tracker (0.6 mm apart). Grasp: the servo pressed the fingers into the board (contact Fz 32.5 N, close F -50.9 N) and closed to 9 mm. At t=5.96 (k05) the orange rod is between the fingers above the board, with the lifted hand in the global view. The grasp fit says rod ctr z 0.082, but its measured top end is about 5 mm off the prediction, so the rod sits slightly askew in the grip. At t=9.56 (k07) the rod is still in the fingers and the tracker follows the hand (z 0.154). Insert: it planned psi 45 deg with tcp z dir [0.64,0.77,0.06] and ran a 126-deg rotation in 12 move_to_joints steps. Three steps failed at t~14.28 (err 0.044) before the rest completed. In the wrist view (k11 t=14.28, k16 t=18.84, k19 t=22.32) the rod keeps the same place and angle between the fingers, so it did not slip or pivot in the hand. Yet in the global view at t=18.84, 22.32 and 24.92 (k16/k19/k21) the rod sticks out horizontally from the gripper beside the blue fixture instead of hanging vertically. So the rod was held rigidly, but the planned 'vertical' hand pose did not put the rod vertical. The camera agrees: tilt 69.97 deg, xy error (-24,-26) mm, bottom 7.3 mm off. The alignment refused to correct an error that large, and insert declared FAIL at t=24.92. The FAIL reason 'rod not in hand / alignment failed' is a combined message; the true cause is the wrong orientation, not a lost rod. After the policy stopped, the rod came out of the hand: the sheet shows it tilting in the wrist view at t~29 and gone by t~32. In final.png it lies flat on the board next to the fixture. It never entered the bore.

locate.evidence: Fit ctr [0.577,0.004,0.013], axis horizontal, 49.2 mm, rms 0.17 mm, n=3384; agrees with the tracker (0.6 mm) and with the rod lying on the board in the t=0 frame.

grasp.evidence: k05 t=5.96 and k07 t=9.56: the rod is in the fingers and lifted with the hand; the tracker rises to z 0.154 with the TCP. Fresh fit ctr z 0.082, 5 mm from the TCP in xy. The rod is slightly askew in the grip (measured top end ~5 mm off the prediction) and the close pushed the board at -51 N.

insert.evidence: The rod stayed fixed in the hand through the 126-deg reorientation (same position in the wrist view at k11/k16/k19; three move_to_joints FAILs at t~14.28, err 0.044, then it completed). The resulting pose left the rod roughly horizontal: the global view at t=18.84-24.92 shows it sticking out sideways, and the camera measured 70 deg tilt and 24-26 mm xy error. Alignment gave up and declared FAIL at t=24.92 without any descent into the bore. Afterwards the rod dropped out (t~29-32) and in final.png it lies on the board beside the fixture.

s01.note: t=0 locate fit the rod lying at ctr [0.378,0.186,0.013] along -y (49.8 mm, rms 0.17 mm), close to the blue fixture; this matches the t=0 frame. Grasp: the servo touched the board (Fz 35 N), the close came out light (F ~0.6 N) and the width ended at only 3.4 mm. At t=6.96 (k04) and t=8.56 (k06) the global view shows the orange rod crosswise in the fingers, lifted off the board. The grasp verifier's fit (ctr z 0.083, 0 mm from the TCP) is consistent with that. The tracker, though, stayed at z ~-0.002 after the lift (t=6.96 onward), so it lost the rod. Insert: during the high transfer move to the fixture (t=8.56 to 11.08) the rod fell out of the hand. At k07 t=11.08 the gripper width is -0.0002 (fully closed on nothing). Both views show the rod lying across the top of the blue fixture, not in the fingers. The insert stage then ran its whole reorientation empty-handed: 6 move_to_joints FAILs ending at t=18.28 (err 0.046), the remaining steps complete by t=23.12, then a descent to z 0.077 at t=25.52. The camera found the rod off the fixture axis, lying (tilt 89.8 deg, xy error (-15,-31) mm). Insert declared FAIL at t=25.76; the true cause is that the rod was dropped during the transfer. The sheet (t=21-40) and final show the rod lying on/beside the fixture top, never in the bore.

locate.evidence: Fit ctr [0.378,0.186,0.013], axis [-0.01,-1,0], 49.8 mm, rms 0.17 mm, n=2747; matches the lying rod in the t=0 frame and the tracker (0.4 mm).

grasp.evidence: k04 t=6.96 and k06 t=8.56: the rod is held crosswise in the fingers and lifted with the hand. Fresh fit ctr z 0.083, centred on the TCP. The grip was weak: close force ~0.6 N, width only 3.4 mm, and the rod fell on the next move. The tracker lost the rod (it kept reporting z -0.002).

insert.evidence: The rod fell from the hand during the high transfer move between t=8.56 (held, k06) and t=11.08 (k07: it lies across the top of the blue fixture, gripper width -0.0002). The insert stage still did the full reorientation and descent with an empty hand (6 joint-move FAILs up to t=18.28) before the camera check failed at t=25.76: the rod was found lying (tilt 89.8 deg, 15/31 mm off). At the end the rod lies on/beside the fixture, not in the bore.
